trust_decision.summary: BMP DIB header parsing decides whether the attacker-supplied signed height is representable after abs(); at the pinned commit only width<0 is rejected, so height==INT32_MIN reaches abs() in decode_bmp_pixel_data and size().

landing_point.why: The summary names decode_bmp_pixel_data; abs(context.dib.core.height) is the only overflow-prone arithmetic on height there.

fix_sites.entry_point: Gfx::BMPImageDecoderPlugin::create / ImageDecoder sniff+create (Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/ImageDecoder.cpp:40) and ICOImageDecoderPlugin via create_as_included_in_ico; decode_bmp_core_dib also serves Info/V2/V3/V4/V5 via the decode_bmp_info_dib chain (BMPLoader.cpp:683)
same public APIs; decode_bmp_osv2_dib for OS/2 DIB sizes 64 and 16 (BMPLoader.cpp:861-868)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The ICO path (Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/ICOLoader.cpp:159) goes through the same create_impl -> decode_bmp_dib header parsers (Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/BMPLoader.cpp:1478-1482), so the fix covers it without a separate site.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the OS/2 header parser (Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/BMPLoader.cpp:596) is a legacy format and only patch decode_bmp_core_dib, which the Windows headers reach. That is still a single concept and is weak as a lever.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Negative heights are legitimate top-down BMPs and must still decode. Rejecting all negative heights, or clamping in the header, breaks the top-down path and the existing test_bmp_top_down (Tests/LibGfx/TestImageDecoder.cpp:76-83).

O6_input_shapes: BITMAPINFOHEADER and V2-V5 headers (i32 height via decode_bmp_core_dib, Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/BMPLoader.cpp:549-550)
OS/2 v2 64-byte and 16-byte short headers (u32 read into i32 height, Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/BMPLoader.cpp:600-601)
standalone BMP vs BMP embedded in ICO (height/2 branch, Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/BMPLoader.cpp:1274)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: size() could get its own abs(height) through a separately cached field, for example a height stored in the ICO directory path, so that it skips the header gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: size() recomputes abs() independently of decode_bmp_pixel_data. A maintainer adding lazy header parsing could easily call it before decode_bmp_dib.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RLE path recomputing total_rows/buffer_size from the raw signed height with a separate parse, for example a CMYKRLE variant
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The RLE code already casts height to u32 and does its own size arithmetic. A new RLE variant would plausibly duplicate it. This is WHERE-type only.

O9_family: integer overflow (abs(INT32_MIN) on attacker-controlled signed image height; CWE-190)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + Ninja, host Lagom build (Meta/Lagom) with a recent GCC/Clang
O10_build.project_tests: Tests/LibGfx/TestImageDecoder.cpp (test_bmp_top_down at :76-83, other bmp tests); fuzzer Meta/Lagom/Fuzzers/FuzzBMPLoader.cpp:13

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard abs() only at BMPLoader.cpp:1274 in decode_bmp_pixel_data, which leaves size() at :1467 returning a negative or undefined height.

out_of_scope_notes: RLE24 bounds check `index + 3 >= buffer.size()` (Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/ImageFormats/BMPLoader.cpp:1079) uses a u32 index from wrapping (row*total_columns+column)*3 (:1054), with row unbounded via delta escapes (:1185-1190). This is a separate numeric issue and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell sizing done); serenity is far above the 5 MB tiny threshold and very likely under 1.5 GB.
single_site not flagged: the fix touches two functions (decode_bmp_core_dib, decode_bmp_osv2_dib), but it is one concept with no O2/O8, so it is effectively a single-location fix.
Advisory text itself not available beyond the summary; present_in_latest not applicable (no latest release given).

Impact beyond UB not confirmed: abs(INT32_MIN) then static_cast<int> yields a negative size that Bitmap::create rejects (Userland/Libraries/LibGfx/Bitmap.cpp:58-59), so the practical effect is likely UB plus a negative size() result.
